narrativeBlocks.title: The sentence
narrativeBlocks.body: Heracles does not labour for glory at first — he labours for a sentence. In a fit of god-sent madness he kills his own children; the oracle at Delphi orders him to serve King Eurystheus and perform the tasks set him. The labours are penance, not ambition.

narrativeBlocks.title: The famous twelve
narrativeBlocks.body: The canonical list: the Nemean lion, the Lernaean hydra, the Ceryneian hind, the Erymanthian boar, the Augean stables, the Stymphalian birds, the Cretan bull, the man-eating mares of Diomedes, the Amazons' girdle, the cattle of Geryon, the apples of the Hesperides, and Cerberus dragged up from the underworld.

narrativeBlocks.title: Not always clean strength
narrativeBlocks.body: The labours are not all fights. The Hydra needs a cauterising ally; the Augean stables are cleaned in a day by diverting two rivers — labour as engineering, not muscles. Several 'labours' are errands or tricks, which is part of their interest.

narrativeBlocks.title: Eurystheus's moving goalposts
narrativeBlocks.body: The cowardly king hides in a bronze jar when Heracles returns, and disqualifies labours on technicalities — helped with the Hydra? doesn't count. Cleaned the stables for payment? doesn't count. Ten becomes twelve.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why a catalogue endures
narrativeBlocks.body: The list is the story: each labour is a self-contained trial a listener can hold in memory. Together they map a hero who conquers not just monsters but geography — the labours literally walk him across the known world and below it.

quiz.prompt: Why does Heracles owe the labours?

choices.text: He killed his own children in a fit of god-sent madness; the oracle sentences him to serve Eurystheus as penance
He volunteered to prove Zeus wrong
Eurystheus is his rival for the throne
The labours are a bride-price for Deianira

quiz.explanation: The labours are penance for kin-killing under madness — the darkest possible origin for the hero.

quiz.prompt: Which labour shows the list isn't all fighting?

choices.text: The Augean stables — cleaned by diverting two rivers through them, a feat of engineering not strength
The Amazons' girdle — taken by force
Cerberus — carried bodily from the underworld

quiz.explanation: Several labours are errands or tricks; the stables are the clearest case of brains over brawn.
